name: Adam Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, independent of employers, AI companies, unions and government. This is confidential. What did your workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and have a bachelor’s degree and a professional accountancy qualification. I prepare garage accounts and tax returns at a firm, and I have enough experience for ordinary files, though the senior handles hard tax disputes. I like tracing a fuel invoice to the bank entry; I get worn down when a client drops the missing page on filing day.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How do work and home meet at the end of the day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Mae, my partner, drives a school minibus, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My pay is about normal for this accountant role, we have about three months of expenses saved, and there are some similar jobs nearby. I have never used AI tools; I prefer a paid demonstration and a clear person responsible before changing a process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm a quick sort of supplier bills is useful only if a person can trace each item. Our repair-garage clients ask why a figure changed, not how fast the screen filled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our pay covers the mortgage and we have about three months saved, so I expect my job to stay sound here. I would still watch any new check that touches the simple account work I do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep reviewing garage accounts and tax returns against the paper source list. In the first year I would ask the manager for a paid demonstration on a closed file if a new check becomes compulsory in writing, but I would not use AI on my own.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the next payslip and mildly bothered by new steps I cannot explain. The old list catches mistakes I know I make.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which mistake does the list catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A garage sent a fuel invoice dated after year end, and I nearly entered it in the wrong period. My list made me check the date before the senior reviewer signed the return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why insist on a demonstration?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used AI tools and prefer a colleague to show the source before I touch client data. I would learn a required process during paid hours, not from a sales video at home.

say: I would keep a **traceable bill** behind each sorted entry.
I would answer clients about **changed figures**, not praise screen speed.
think: Our **three-month cushion** and normal pay make this world stable.
A new check could touch my **simple account work**.
do: Keep reviewing **garage accounts** and returns against the paper source list.
Learn a **required AI check** only after written job rule and paid closed-file demonstration.
feel: I feel **calm** about income but wary of unexplained new steps.
S0.quote: Our repair-garage clients ask why a figure changed, not how fast the screen filled.
fieldNote: His **paper list** caught an out-of-period fuel invoice, making his caution about source dates concrete.
He has **never used AI** but will learn a compulsory process after written instruction and a paid demonstration.

steps.text: Keep reviewing garage accounts with paper invoice and date checks
Learn required AI check after written rule and paid closed-file demonstration

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the manager to keep a named accountant on each tax return and a real training path for apprentices. If software writes the first draft, somebody must still teach why a garage invoice belongs in one year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing notes and checking accounts fill much of my week, so some paid hours could shrink. My partner’s wage and three months saved give us a little room, and there are some local firms, but the mortgage still needs a full month’s pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for a written rota forecast and keep checking assigned accounts. If the firm makes its approved checker a written duty, I would take paid old-file training beside the senior; if my hours are cut in the first year, I would apply for posted local accountant roles only with written salary, hours and a start date that protect the mortgage while I keep my current shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a possible pay cut, even though it is not a certainty. I would rather learn one required process than jump firms on a rumour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who teaches the apprentices now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our senior reviewer goes through mistakes with them on Friday mornings. I would ask the manager to keep that paid hour. A video cannot notice the question a trainee is afraid to ask.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the posted job starts on school afternoons?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Mae drives a school minibus and can collect our younger child only when her route ends before three. I would ask for written start and finish times before accepting a local offer.

say: I would keep **named tax sign-off** and paid apprentice teaching.
I would ask for a **written rota forecast** before cuts.
think: My **writing and checking hours** could shrink.
A **three-month reserve** and some local firms give limited room to move.
do: Keep **assigned accounts** and ask the manager for a written rota forecast.
Learn the **approved checker** only with written duty and paid senior-supervised old-file training.
After lost hours, seek **posted local accounting work** with written mortgage wage and start times fitting Mae’s conditional pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible cut but can respond deliberately.
S1.quote: A video cannot notice the question a trainee is afraid to ask.
fieldNote: His **apprenticeship concern** points to an existing paid Friday review, not a vague claim about tradition.
The **new job gate** is concrete: written mortgage-covering pay, start/finish times and pickup only when Mae’s route ends early.

steps.text: Keep assigned garage accounts while asking for written rota forecast
Learn required checker on paid old files with senior only after written duty
Seek posted role after cuts with written mortgage wage and hours; retain shifts until school-compatible start
Require written start/finish times and pickup only if Mae’s minibus route ends before three

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2028 reaches tax and accounts screens in 2028, before capable robots arrive around 2031. The firm owes us a real date for any staffing change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of my return checks to disappear when cheaper AGI can think through them, and my job could go. Three months of expenses would not last through a long search if nearby firms cut together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for written cut dates and stop paying for the family’s weekend film club at renewal, keeping the fee for bills; Mae is home with the children then, so childcare is unaffected. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I would apply for posted accounts jobs at local repair depots only with written wage, hours and start date covering the mortgage; if none is open, I would keep any paid firm files and ask Mae about confirmed extra minibus runs that still leave school pickup covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about losing the household wage I bring in. The three-month cushion is breathing room, not a replacement job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Mae get the extra runs?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school might ask her to cover another route, but only its written rota and paid rate count. We would not take an extra run if it leaves the younger child waiting outside school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the film club first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is an evening leisure club we all attend together, not a place that watches the children. We can borrow films and still have a family night without paying the membership.

say: I would say **AGI by 2028** reaches our tax desks before capable robots.
I would ask for **written cut dates** for staff.
think: I expect most **return checks** to disappear after 2028.
Three months saved may not last if **local firms** cut together.
do: Cancel the **family film club** at renewal and retain the fee for bills.
After job loss, seek **posted depot accounts work** with written mortgage wage, hours and start date.
If none opens, keep **paid firm files** and discuss Mae’s confirmed extra runs only with school pickup covered.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely lost wages and a fixed mortgage.
S2.quote: The three-month cushion is breathing room, not a replacement job.
fieldNote: He names the **2028 desk date** and knows robots later will not spare account checks.
The **club cut** leaves childcare intact because parents attend; Mae’s extra bus pay requires confirmed rota, rate and pickup.

steps.text: Cancel family leisure film club at renewal and retain fee for bills
Seek posted depot accounts after job loss with written mortgage wage, hours and start date
Keep paid firm files if no suitable depot vacancy opens
Discuss Mae’s extra runs only if no depot vacancy, with confirmed paid rota and school pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2031 gives us time to learn what clients will still pay an accountant to explain. The robots around 2034 do not move the desk-work deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years could let us save another mortgage payment and test some client meetings, though routine return checking still looks exposed in 2031. I would not buy a course because somebody says it is the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the partner to let me join a paid monthly meeting with two garage owners, with the senior handling technical advice and the client fee covering my hours. I would add 90 a month to savings while both wages hold; in the first year after 2031, if my tax hours fall, I would stay only if both garage owners renew at fees covering my salary, or apply for advertised local accountant posts with written pay and hours no worse than now while keeping paid firm files.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the tax hours but able to check whether clients really pay. Five years is enough time to count renewals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you bring to the meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show the owners which unpaid parts invoices are pressing their cash. My senior would check the tax advice, because I handle ordinary accounts but am not the person for the hardest case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the partner refuses paid meetings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep reviewing returns and ask for the written hours plan. I would not take unpaid evening calls to make the idea look viable.

say: I would test **paid garage meetings** before 2031.
I would remind staff **2034 robots** come after the tax desk change.
think: Routine **tax-return checks** may shrink when AGI reaches my desk in 2031.
Paid **garage renewals** need to cover my wage.
do: Join **paid monthly meetings** with two garage owners, approval and senior checks; otherwise keep returns and request written hours.
Save **90 monthly** while both wages hold.
After lost tax hours, stay only if **both garages renew** at salary-covering fees or seek written equal-pay local work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about future hours while able to test paid demand.
S3.quote: I would not take unpaid evening calls to make the idea look viable.
fieldNote: His **paid meeting test** requires partner approval and senior advice, matching his ordinary rather than expert technical skill.
If **meetings are refused**, he keeps current returns; any outside move needs advertised work with written equal pay and hours.

steps.text: Join approved paid monthly meetings with two garages and senior checks; otherwise retain returns/request written hours
Save 90 monthly while both household wages hold
Stay salaried after cuts only if both garages renew at fees covering wage
Seek advertised local post with written equal pay/hours while retaining paid files if meetings fail

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2036 gives a decade to reduce our mortgage and see whether garage owners pay for explanation work. The robots around 2039 do not delay tax desk changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years could bring the balance down and make the children more independent if both wages keep coming. I still expect AGI to take routine tax checks in 2036; the client meeting fee must be real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep preparing accounts and ask for paid quarterly garage meetings with senior review, if the partner and clients approve. I would first build six months of expenses in cash with 110 monthly deposits while both wages hold, then add extra mortgage principal; in the first year after 2036, if return hours fall, I would stay only if paid client renewals cover my wage, or take a posted local role after written pay, hours and a start date that fit school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about 2036 but secure enough over the next few years. I want a reserve before paying down a loan I cannot draw from.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why save cash before mortgage principal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A lower debt balance cannot buy groceries after a missed wage. Six months of cash would keep us from treating every small shock as a family emergency.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask the children to change school?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a real job offer with written pay and a start date, if a move became necessary. I would not move them for a possible client renewal.

say: I would test **paid garage renewals** before relying on them.
I would use **ten years** to build cash and lower mortgage debt.
think: Routine **tax checks** remain exposed when AGI reaches my screen in 2036.
The **mortgage balance** can fall only while both wages continue.
do: Keep **accounts** and test paid quarterly garage meetings only with partner, client and senior approval.
Save **110 monthly** to six months cash before extra principal while both wages hold.
After lost return hours, stay only with **wage-covering renewals** or take posted work with written pay, hours and start.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about 2036 while nearer-term wages look secure.
S4.quote: I want a reserve before paying down a loan I cannot draw from.
fieldNote: His **cash-first plan** protects a six-month reserve before extra mortgage principal payments.
The **outside move** needs a real offer, written pay and start date before considering the children’s school.

steps.text: Test paid quarterly garage meetings only with partner, client and senior approval
Save 110 monthly to six months cash before extra principal while wages hold
Stay salaried after cuts only if paid garage renewals cover wage
Take posted local role with written pay/hours/start fitting pickup before any necessary school change

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because routine tax checks could disappear before I know what other paid work is real. Written notice, paid client meetings and an actual local vacancy would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who teaches the new accountant to notice the date on a fuel invoice. A fast draft can still put the bill in the wrong year.

headlineQuote: A fast draft can still put the bill in the wrong year.
portrait: At **43**, Adam is an experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who handles garage files.
He and **partner Mae** have two school-age children, a mortgage, typical pay and about three months saved.
He has **never used AI**, values paid apprentice teaching and can consider some local accounting jobs.
The **2028 deadline** threatens routine checks; longer runways allow paid client meetings and conditional cash savings.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his routine tax checks before replacement paid work is ready.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice**, paid client meetings and a real local vacancy.
